 Order

The present revision petition is filed under Section 397, 401 of Cr.P.C. challenging the order dated 7.11.2016 passed by the Special Judge S.C./S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and First Additional Sessions Judge Vidisha in Case No.600121/16 (criminal revision) by which the order dated 23.09.2015 passed by the learned JMFC Vidisha in Case No.R.T. 3436/06 was quashed.

entities.text: Special Judge S.C./S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The facts in brief to decide the petition are that the complainant/Food Inspector filed a complaint under Sections 2(ix) (G) (J) (K), 7(II), 7(v) read with Section 16(1) (a) (i) (ii) of Prevention of Food Preetam Singh Jadon vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 7 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174518270/
1 Adulteration Act, 1954 [in short the Act] alleging that on 26.05.2003 the co- accused Manoj Sahu was found to be in possession of the adulterated and misbranded Thrush Cola,
sweetened carbonated beverages, Thrush orange sweetened carbonated beverages and packaged drinking water.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Preetam Singh Jadon vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the allegations in the complaint, the dealer of the said adulterated items is M/s. Jadon & Company and the present petitioner/accused is the proprietor of that company which was selling the above adulterated food.

The learned trial Court after taking evidence before charge opined that prima facie the involvement of the present petitioner/accused was not found to be proved and discharged him by its order dated 23.09.2015.
However, the learned revisional Court by its impugned order allowed the revision filed by the respondent and quashed the order passed by the learned trial Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the impugned order is perverse and contrary to the settled principles of law.
It is further argued that the learned trial Court has rightly discharged the present petitioner as there is no evidence on record to show the involvement of the petitioner in committing the crime.
It is further argued that the learned revisional Court has passed the order on the basis of documents which are not admissible in evidence because the original were not filed before the Court below.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent argued that the impugned order is in accordance with law and need not be interfered with.
Heard and perused the record.

The Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan vs. Fatehkaran Mehdu, reported in (2017) 3 SCC 198 has observed that at the stage of framing of a charge, the court is concerned not with proof of allegation, rather it has to focus on material and form an opinion whether there is strong suspicion that accused has committed an offence, which if put to trial, could prove his guilt.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan vs. Fatehkaran Mehdu, reported in (2017) 3 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Framing of charge is not a stage, at which stage final test of guilt is to be applied.
Power of quashing criminal proceedings particularly, charge framed in terms of Section 228 Cr.p.C. should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases.
The Court should apply the test as to whether uncontroverted allegations as made from record of case and documents submitted therewith, prima facie establish the offence or not.
The same principle has been laid down in the case of P. Vijayan vs. The State of Kerala, 2010 (2) SCC 398.

entities.text: P. Vijayan vs. The State of Kerala, 2010 (2) SCC 398
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is therefore well settled that at the stage of framing of charge, the court is only required to see whether a prima facie case has been made out or not.
At the stage of framing of charge, the evidentiary value of the documents are not required to be seen.

In the present case on the basis of the allegations made in the complaint as well as the documents filed by the respondent/complainant i.e. report of the Public Analyst Ex-P/42 along with Ex-D/1 (the licence issued by the Municipal Corporation Bhopal), Ex-D/2 (details of Trade Mark THRUSH),
Ex-D/3 (letter from the Goodwill informing the petitioner/accused regarding registration of Trade Mark) and Ex-D/4 (Receipt No.178370 of Trade Marks Registry), the involvement of the petitioner/accused in the crime is prima facie found to be proved for taking cognizance against him Preetam Singh Jadon vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 7 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174518270/
2 under the relevant Sections as mentioned above of the Act.

entities.text: Preetam Singh Jadon vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, the impugned order is found to be in accordance with the settled principles of law and does not require any interference.
Accordingly, this revision petition is dismissed.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE Van VANDANA VERMA 2022.07.09 10:47:20 -07'00'

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Framing of charge is not a stage, at which stage final test of guilt is to be applied.
Power of quashing criminal proceedings particularly, charge framed in terms of Section 228 Cr.p.C. should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases.
The Court should apply the test as to whether uncontroverted allegations as made from record of case and documents submitted therewith, prima facie establish the offence or not.
The same principle has been laid down in the case of P. Vijayan vs. The State of Kerala, 2010 (2) SCC 398.
It is therefore well settled that at the stage of framing of charge, the court is only required to see whether a prima facie case has been made out or not.
At the stage of framing of charge, the evidentiary value of the documents are not required to be seen.
